summary.title: From NAND to Tetris: Building a Modern Computer From First Principles
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source course and project set for building a general-purpose computer and software hierarchy from logic gates up, based on The Elements of Computing Systems.
keywords: building a computer from first principles
takeaways: The course walks through building a general-purpose computer system and software hierarchy from the ground up.
Materials (lectures, projects, tools) are free and open-source for non-profit use.
You can self-study by working through the lecture notes and Projects section, or take the paid Coursera version with a completion certificate.
The course is used at 400+ universities, high schools, and bootcamps.
Instructors can contact the maintainers for additional course materials.
summary.summary: This is the home page for the Nand to Tetris course, companion to the book The Elements of Computing Systems by Noam Nisan and Shimon Schocken (MIT Press). It describes the course as a set of lectures, project materials, and tools for building a general-purpose computer and a modern software stack from the ground up. The materials are free and open-source for non-profit use, and self-learners can work through the lecture notes and Projects section. A paid Coursera version with a completion certificate is also mentioned. The page does not list specific technologies, languages, or a detailed syllabus beyond a link to one.
